title: Lambdas capture locals by value
description: A lambda copies each captured local when it is created: later reassignments in the outer function are invisible to it, and assignments inside the lambda only change that call's argument copy (not persisted even between calls of the same lambda), so counters, accumulators and flags silently stay unchanged; only shared reference types (Array, Dictionary, Object) appear to work.
example: var n := 0 ⏎ var inc := func(): n += 1 ⏎ inc.call() ⏎ print(n)  # 0 (warning CONFUSABLE_CAPTURE_REASSIGNMENT)
evidence_issues: #69014 (closed not planned, 3 reactions, 14 comments) | #70549 (closed not planned, 0 reactions, 1 comment) | #93070 (closed by godot-docs PR #9556, 0 reactions, 2 comments) | #93922 (closed not planned, 0 reactions, 1 comment) | #117348 (open, 0 reactions, 4 comments) | godot-proposals #8558 'Capture local variables consistently' (open, 10 reactions, 19 comments)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html (Lambda functions): "Local variables are captured by value once, when the lambda is created. So they won't be updated in the lambda if reassigned in the outer function" | same section: "a lambda cannot reassign an outer local variable. After exiting the lambda, the variable will be unchanged, because the lambda capture implicitly shadows it" (godot-docs 0914a4d gdscript_basics.rst:1574-1586)
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:2687-2691 (OPCODE_CREATE_LAMBDA copies every captured value into a Vector<Variant> at creation) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_lambda_callable.cpp:104-105,120 (captures are passed as leading call arguments) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:547-549 (callee copies each argument into its own stack slot, so writes never reach the stored capture) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:2931-2951 (CONFUSABLE_CAPTURE_REASSIGNMENT only for assignments inside the lambda; nothing for an outer reassignment after capture) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_warning.h:89,149 (WARN by default)
frequency: 5 independent bug reports of the same by-design behaviour 2022-2026 (GraphQL searches 'lambda in:title variable' and 'lambda capture' in godotengine/godot, triaged by hand) plus proposal #8558; a docs warning (godot-docs PR #9556) and a dedicated warning (PR #93691) were both added in 4.3 in response; forum.godotengine.org t/108011 asks the same
fix_reason: Capture semantics are the language's own definition: capture by reference through boxed cells (or reject mutation of captured locals at compile time), implemented with its own CallableCustom (callable_custom_create2, core/extension/gdextension_interface.json:8375); no engine behaviour involved.

title: Lambda lifetime: self-capturing lambdas leak RefCounted owners; freed captures become null
description: A lambda that uses self or a member inside a RefCounted script keeps a strong Ref to its owner, so storing it on the owner (e.g. connecting it to the owner's own signal) forms a cycle that is never freed and shows up only as anonymous 'Leaked instance' lines at exit; for non-RefCounted owners the lambda keeps a raw pointer, and captured objects that were freed are silently replaced by null with an error print.
example: extends RefCounted ⏎ signal changed ⏎ func _init(): changed.connect(func(): print(self))  # instance never freed
evidence_issues: #102327 (open, 4 reactions, 7 comments) | #79707 (closed, crash on freed instance fixed by PR #81605 in 4.2, 1 reaction, 1 comment) | #117840 (open, 0 reactions, 0 comments: freed-capture error confusing) | #97523 (open, confirmed, 0 reactions, 6 comments: method callables do not keep self alive, potential use-after-free)
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript_lambda_callable.cpp:285-291 (self lambda on a RefCounted owner stores Ref<RefCounted> reference = p_self, a strong ref) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_lambda_callable.cpp:296-301 (other owners stored as raw Object*) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_lambda_callable.cpp:106-112 (error 'Lambda capture at index %d was freed. Passed "null" instead.') | modules/gdscript/gdscript_lambda_callable.cpp:217-222 (invalid-instance check only under DEBUG_ENABLED)
frequency: low reactions but recurring: 4 reports via GraphQL title search 'lambda' plus self/free/leak in godotengine/godot; a #102327 commenter is 'removing almost all lambdas from the codebase' to stop the leaks
fix_reason: What a closure retains is a language decision (explicit capture lists, weak self by ObjectID, compile-time error for a self-capturing lambda stored on self), implemented through the language's own CallableCustom whose object id and validity use ObjectID (GDExtensionCallableCustomInfo2 at core/extension/gdextension_interface.json:2460, object_get_instance_from_id at :7960), all public GDExtension API.

title: Object types are implicitly nullable; no null safety
description: Every Object-typed variable, parameter and return value accepts null without annotation and the analyzer never tracks nullness, so missing nodes and resources surface only as runtime 'null instance' errors (the most common GDScript runtime error); conversely built-in value types can never be null, so an optional int or Vector2 needs Variant or a sentinel.
example: var target: Enemy = null ⏎ target.take_damage(1)  # compiles; fails at runtime on a null instance
evidence_issues: godot-proposals #162 'Add support for nullable static types in GDScript' (open, 1038 reactions, 280 comments) | godot-proposals #11054 'Make objects non-nullable by default' (open, 72 reactions, 9 comments) | godot-proposals #1321 null-coalescing operator (open, 179 reactions, 38 comments) | godot-proposals #1902 safe navigation operator (open, 152 reactions, 3 comments) | godot-proposals #12310 (open, 15 reactions, 5 comments: 'Attempt to call function on null instance is our most common runtime error')
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html (null): "Only types that inherit from Object can have a null value (Object is therefore called a "nullable" type)." (godot-docs 0914a4d gdscript_basics.rst:709-710)
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:6460-6462 (check_type_compatibility: 'null is acceptable in object') | modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:149,462 (runtime 'Attempt to call ... on a null instance.' and 'Cannot call method ... on a null value.') | core/variant/type_info.h:54 and core/extension/extension_api_dump.cpp:92 (METADATA_OBJECT_IS_REQUIRED / argument meta 'required' marks some engine Object parameters and returns as non-null via RequiredParam/RequiredResult; 215 occurrences in core/scene/servers headers, so coverage is partial)
frequency: #162 is the 2nd most-reacted topic:gdscript proposal (GraphQL dump of all 941 such proposals sorted by reactions); forum.godotengine.org search for "null instance" returns at least 350 topics (12 result pages, more remaining); Stack Overflow questions matching 'null instance': 25 tagged godot, 17 tagged gdscript (api.stackexchange.com search/advanced total)
fix_reason: Non-null-by-default object types with explicit T? and flow-sensitive null checks are language and analyzer rules; engine API nullability can be seeded from the extension_api.json 'required' metadata, and unannotated engine returns must be typed nullable conservatively (toolchain data, no engine change).

title: 'as' cast silently yields null
description: For object types, x as T returns null instead of failing when x is an object of another class, so a wrong cast surfaces later and elsewhere as a null-instance error; with a built-in target type the same syntax raises a runtime error instead, and 'as Array[T]' on typed arrays does not convert as expected.
example: var player := body as Player  # null when body is an Enemy; the error appears only at player.hp
evidence_issues: #54311 'Type casting (as) not working with typed arrays' (open, confirmed, crash, 8 reactions, 3 comments; fix PR #124662 open) | #72627 'Cannot cast typed arrays using type hints' (closed as duplicate of #54311, 39 reactions, 8 comments)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/static_typing.html: "The as keyword silently casts the variable to null in case of a type mismatch at runtime, without an error/warning. While this may be convenient in some cases, it can also lead to bugs." | same page: "If you try to cast with a built-in type and it fails, Godot will throw an error." (godot-docs 0914a4d static_typing.rst:317-319,355) | https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html (Casting): "If the value is not a subtype, the casting operation will result in a null value." (gdscript_basics.rst:1301)
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:1665-1666 (OPCODE_CAST_TO_NATIVE: '*dst = Variant(); // invalid cast, assign NULL') | modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:1714-1717 (OPCODE_CAST_TO_SCRIPT: same) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:1630-1637 (OPCODE_CAST_TO_BUILTIN errors, but only under DEBUG_ENABLED)
frequency: the docs carry an explicit 'can lead to bugs' note; typed-array variant: #72627 (39 reactions) plus #54311; no phrase-specific forum count possible (the failure has no distinctive error message)
fix_reason: The language can split a checked cast (fails loudly on mismatch) from a conditional cast returning T? that the type checker forces to be null-checked, and define container conversions explicitly; all compiled by the language.

title: Variant values flow into typed code unchecked; UNSAFE_* warnings off by default
description: Typing is opt-in per declaration, and any Variant-typed expression (untyped variable, untyped Array or Dictionary element, Variant-returning engine method such as Object.get or Array.front, chained property access) is accepted wherever a concrete type is expected and checked only at runtime; the warnings that would flag this (UNSAFE_PROPERTY_ACCESS, UNSAFE_METHOD_ACCESS, UNSAFE_CAST, UNSAFE_CALL_ARGUMENT, UNTYPED_DECLARATION) are ignored by default, so a project that looks typed can still contain unchecked calls.
example: var cfg := {"hp": 10} ⏎ var hp: String = cfg["hp"]  # compiles (Variant source); fails at runtime
evidence_issues: godot-proposals #173 force static typing (closed by PR #81355 adding the optional UNTYPED_DECLARATION warning in 4.2, 65 reactions, 34 comments) | #60499 false-positive UNSAFE_PROPERTY_ACCESS (open, 11 reactions, 6 comments) | #86300 UNSAFE_METHOD_ACCESS for autoloads (open, 12 reactions, 15 comments) | #59721 typed arrays lose their type through Variant-returning functions (open, 9 reactions, 6 comments)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/static_typing.html (Warning system): "We have a number of warnings aimed specifically at users of typed GDScript. By default, these warnings are disabled" | same: "Currently, UNSAFE_* warnings do not cover all cases that unsafe lines cover." (godot-docs 0914a4d static_typing.rst:469-478) | https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html (Arrays): "array methods like front() and back() still have the Variant return type" (gdscript_basics.rst:878-879)
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:6414-6416 (a Variant source is compatible with any target: 'This is acceptable but unsafe') | modules/gdscript/gdscript_warning.h:124-129 (UNTYPED_DECLARATION, INFERRED_DECLARATION and UNSAFE_* default to IGNORE: 'Too common in untyped scenarios')
frequency: forum.godotengine.org exact phrase "UNSAFE_PROPERTY_ACCESS": 6 topics; the issues above have 9-12 reactions each; #173 65 reactions
fix_reason: A statically typed language makes 'any' explicit and requires a checked conversion where it meets a concrete type (compile error otherwise); Variant-returning engine methods still need modelled return types, which is toolchain data from extension_api.json, not an engine change.

title: No type narrowing after an 'is' check
description: Inside 'if x is Player:' the analyzer still types x as its declared type, so member access in the branch is unchecked and loses completion; users add a redundant 'as' cast or a second variable, and code that relies on the check stays untyped.
example: func hit(b: Node2D): ⏎   if b is Player: ⏎     b.take_damage(1)  # not type-checked; UNSAFE_METHOD_ACCESS when enabled
evidence_issues: godot-proposals #8530 ignore unsafe access inside 'is' blocks (open, 26 reactions, 10 comments; 2 proposals marked duplicate: #14632, #14804) | godot-proposals #6941 safe type narrowing via match (open, 46 reactions, 19 comments) | #93510 (closed not planned, 0 reactions, 2 comments) | #111923 (closed, consolidated into proposal #6941, 1 reaction, 1 comment)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/static_typing.html: the safe pattern shown is an explicit cast plus null check, "var my_script := node_2d as MyScript" followed by "if my_script != null:" (godot-docs 0914a4d static_typing.rst:600-601)
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:5264-5303 (reduce_type_test types the 'is' expression as bool and checks compatibility; the operand's type inside the guarded block is never refined)
frequency: #8530 and #6941 total 72 reactions; 2 duplicate proposals and 2 closed bug-style reports (GraphQL MARKED_AS_DUPLICATE timeline events and title search)
fix_reason: Flow-sensitive narrowing (smart casts) is purely an analyzer feature; the runtime type test it relies on already exists.

title: Typed arrays are invariant and never convert implicitly
description: Array[T] carries its element type at runtime and assignment requires an exact match: Array[Node2D] cannot be assigned to Array[Node], and untyped arrays (Array.map results, range(), JSON data, literals through a ternary) cannot be assigned to Array[int]; the analyzer accepts untyped-to-typed as merely unsafe, so the failure is a runtime error.
example: var a: Array[int] = [1, 2, 3] ⏎ var b: Array[int] = a.map(func(x): return x * 2)  # runtime: Trying to assign an array of type "Array" to a variable of type "Array[int]"
evidence_issues: #72566 'Array map/filter fail with typed-array variables and functions' (open, 93 reactions, 18 comments; 1 duplicate marked: #100377) | #54311 (open, 8 reactions, 3 comments) with duplicate #72627 (39 reactions, 8 comments) | #72762 range() should return Array[int] (open, 13 reactions, 1 comment) | #83026 empty array through ternary cannot be assigned (open, 10 reactions, 2 comments) | #86851 append of a wrong type silently not added (open, 10 reactions, 15 comments)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html (Typed arrays): "you cannot assign an array with a different element type, even if the type is a subtype of the required type." | same: "The only exception was made for the Array (Array[Variant]) type, for user convenience and compatibility with old code. However, operations on untyped arrays are considered unsafe." (godot-docs 0914a4d gdscript_basics.rst:896-919)
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:6428-6432 (typed element types must be equal) and :6388 (typed vs untyped treated as compatible but unsafe) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:1463-1468 (OPCODE_ASSIGN_TYPED_ARRAY requires identical builtin/class/script element type, else error) | core/variant/array.cpp:648-664 (Array::map returns an untyped Array) vs core/variant/array.cpp:619-622 (filter copies the source type) | core/variant/container_type_validate.h:37-47 (element type identity = variant_type + class_name + script)
frequency: #72566 is the 6th most-reacted topic:gdscript issue in godotengine/godot (GraphQL dump of all 4377 such issues sorted by reactions); forum.godotengine.org exact phrase "Trying to assign an array of type": 9 topics
status: open (#72566, #54311; PR #124662 open; PR #116943 for typed map/filter closed unmerged)
fix_reason: The language can type map/filter/range generically, insert converting copies (Array.assign) at typed boundaries and reject covariant assignment statically; the runtime element-type tag and its exact-match check are Variant/Array semantics that every language meets when typed arrays cross the engine boundary.

title: int/float: integer division and silent narrowing
description: '/' on two ints truncates (5 / 2 == 2) and '%' truncates toward zero; storing a float into an int slot (including a := inferred int) silently truncates; the warnings (INTEGER_DIVISION, NARROWING_CONVERSION) fire only when both static types are known, cannot express intent (INTEGER_DIVISION still fires after an explicit int() cast), and untyped code gets no warning at all.
example: print(5 / 2)  # 2 ⏎ var hp := 3 ⏎ hp -= 0.5  # hp == 2 (inferred int, truncated)
evidence_issues: #42966 'Integer division generates warnings even if you cast' (open, confirmed, 60 reactions, 17 comments; fix PR #107642 open) | godot-proposals #1866 separate integer and real division operators (closed not planned, 96 reactions, 110 comments) | godot-proposals #11998 add an integer division operator (open, 25 reactions, 23 comments) | #75832 'var a := 1; a *= 1.0' printed garbage (closed, regression fixed by PR #75885 in 4.1, 4 reactions, 5 comments)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html (Operators): "If both operands of the / operator are int, then integer division is performed instead of fractional. For example 5 / 2 == 2, not 2.5." | same: "For negative values, the % operator and fmod() use truncation instead of rounding towards negative infinity." (godot-docs 0914a4d gdscript_basics.rst:322-325)
evidence_source: core/variant/variant_op.cpp:353 (OP_DIVIDE INT,INT registered with an int64 result) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:3161-3169 (INTEGER_DIVISION only when both operand static types are int or VectorNi) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:3095-3097 (NARROWING_CONVERSION for a float assigned to a hard int) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:1421-1426 (typed assignment converts with Variant::construct, i.e. truncates)
frequency: forum.godotengine.org exact phrase "integer division": 25 topics (e.g. '-(1/30) returns 0 in GDscript', 'Godot ignores decimal places in division - Why?'); #1866 drew 110 comments; #42966 60 reactions
fix_reason: The language defines its own arithmetic (distinct real and integer division operators, no implicit float-to-int narrowing, explicit conversions) and compiles it itself; Variant OP_DIVIDE matters only if untyped arithmetic is delegated to Variant::evaluate.

title: == between unrelated types is a runtime error
description: '==' and '!=' between values of unrelated types (int vs String, Object vs bool, Array vs int) do not return false but raise 'Invalid operands' at runtime, while some mixed pairs (int/float, String/StringName, anything vs null) are allowed; typed code gets a compile error, but in untyped code (JSON or Dictionary values, Variant returns) the comparison aborts the function.
example: var id = data.get("id")  # sometimes String, sometimes int ⏎ if id == 0: pass  # Invalid operands 'String' and 'int' in operator '=='
root_layer: engine core (Variant operator table) + GDScript language
evidence_issues: #26375 'Allow for comparing variables of different types' (closed, 8 reactions, 4 comments; 11 cross-referencing issues) | godot-proposals #4571 (closed 2023 by PR #71758, which added is_same() instead of changing ==; 7 reactions, 26 comments) | #48150 cannot compare null with int (closed, fixed by PR #52788 in 4.0, 1 reaction, 4 comments)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html (Operators): "The == and != operators sometimes allow you to compare values of different types (for example, 1 == 1.0 is true), but in other cases it can cause a runtime error. If you're not sure about the types of the operands, you can safely use the is_same() function" (godot-docs 0914a4d gdscript_basics.rst:328-329)
evidence_source: core/variant/variant_op.cpp:489-493 (OP_EQUAL registered for INT/INT, INT/FLOAT, FLOAT/INT and the string-like pairs; no INT/STRING entry) | core/variant/variant_op.cpp:571-595 (NIL vs other types: always false) | core/variant/variant_op.cpp:1051-1055 (missing evaluator: r_valid = false) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:756-761 ('Invalid operands ... in operator', then the function aborts) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:3221 (compile-time error only when both types are known)
frequency: forum.godotengine.org exact phrase "in operator '=='": 18 topics; "Invalid operands" (all operators): 117 topics; Stack Overflow "in operator '=='": 6 questions tagged godot
fix_reason: With static types the compiler rejects comparisons between unrelated types, and the language can define == on 'any' to return false for mismatched types instead of erroring; the Variant operator table itself (Variant::evaluate, Expression, engine-side comparisons) stays as is for every language.

title: match, Dictionary keys and 'in' use type-strict equality, unlike ==
description: 1 == 1.0 is true, but match patterns, Dictionary key lookup, Array.has/find/erase and the 'in' operator compare the type first: 1 does not match 1.0, d[2.0] misses a key stored as 2, and 1 in [1.0] is false; numbers parsed from JSON are floats, so int keys and int patterns silently miss; String and StringName are the only cross-type pair treated as equal.
example: var d := {2: "a"} ⏎ print(2 == 2.0, d.has(2.0))  # true false ⏎ match 1.0: ⏎   1: print("never")
root_layer: engine core (Variant hash_compare) + GDScript language (match codegen)
evidence_issues: #82575 'Dictionary Lookups with float/int confusion' (open, 0 reactions, 1 comment) | #71559 'Inconsistent comparison of JSON numeric values' (open, 1 reaction, 0 comments; reports that in Godot 4 '1 in arr' is false for a JSON array) | #80162 int and float equal under == (open, documentation, 0 reactions, 3 comments) | #60145 match strict for String vs StringName (closed by PR #68747 'Unify StringName and String' in 4.0, 2 reactions, 15 comments) | #64171 String and StringName incompatible (closed by PR #68747, 15 reactions, 5 comments)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html (match): "match is more type strict than the == operator. For example 1 will not match 1.0. The only exception is String vs StringName matching" (godot-docs 0914a4d gdscript_basics.rst:1914)
evidence_source: core/variant/variant.cpp:3213-3216 (hash_compare returns false when types differ) | core/variant/variant.cpp:3437-3447 (StringLikeVariantComparator: only String/StringName cross-type) | core/variant/dictionary.cpp:46 (Dictionary is HashMap<Variant, Variant, HashMapHasherDefault, StringLikeVariantComparator>) | core/variant/array.cpp:394 (Array::find uses StringLikeVariantComparator) | core/variant/variant_op.h:1195 ('x in array' is find() != -1) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_compiler.cpp:1455-1479 (a match literal pattern tests typeof equality first, String/StringName exempted)
frequency: low reactions: 5 issues 2022-2023 found via title search (int/float, StringName, JSON); maintainers answer with is_same() or docs rather than changing behaviour (#82575 reply)
fix_reason: A statically typed language can type Dictionary keys, collection elements and match scrutinees so that int/float mixing is a compile error or an explicit conversion, and can define its own match equality; key hashing and equality inside engine Dictionary/Array are Variant semantics every language observes.

title: Enums are plain ints
description: Named enums are int constants: an int is accepted where the enum type is expected (warning only), casts are not validated, an enum-typed variable without a default is 0 even when 0 is not a member, values print as numbers and need keys()/find_key for names, and exported or saved enum values are stored as ints.
example: enum State { IDLE = 1, RUN = 2 } ⏎ var s: State  # 0, not a member (ENUM_VARIABLE_WITHOUT_DEFAULT) ⏎ s = 7  # accepted with warnings
evidence_issues: #20368 named enums could not be used as types (closed, implemented for 4.0, 72 reactions, 33 comments) | #74123 enum export without default shows an invalid value (closed by PR #102743 in 4.4; warning added by PR #90756 in 4.3; 5 reactions, 4 comments) | #56878 enum comparison raised Invalid operands with an enum type hint (closed by PR #57591, 11 reactions, 2 comments) | #31896 simpler way to get enum value names (closed, 27 reactions, 7 comments) | godot-proposals #12954 string-valued enums (open, 10 reactions, 7 comments)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html (Enums): "Enums are basically a shorthand for constants, and are pretty useful if you want to assign consecutive integers to some constant." (godot-docs 0914a4d gdscript_basics.rst:1365-1366)
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:6446-6449 (an int source is accepted for an enum target) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:6378-6381 (only an INT_AS_ENUM_WITHOUT_CAST warning) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:6424-6427 (an enum value is implicitly an int) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_warning.h:81-83,141-143 (INT_AS_ENUM_WITHOUT_CAST, INT_AS_ENUM_WITHOUT_MATCH, ENUM_VARIABLE_WITHOUT_DEFAULT 'The default will be set to 0 instead of the first enum value', all WARN)

fix_reason: The language can make enums nominal types (no implicit int conversion, checked conversion, first member as default, name-aware printing); at the engine boundary they still travel as int (PROPERTY_HINT_ENUM, engine enum parameters, saved scenes), so stored values stay ints.

title: Engine callbacks matched by name only: typos never run, overrides replace the parent
description: Virtual callbacks are looked up by exact method name, so a misspelled override (_proccess, _Ready, _physics_proces) is just a new method that is never called and there is no override keyword to catch it; a correctly named override replaces the base script's implementation (since 4.0 the parent's _ready/_process run only via super()), while _notification is still dispatched to every level; same-named non-virtual engine methods cannot be overridden at all.
example: extends Node ⏎ func _proccess(delta):  # typo: never called, no diagnostic ⏎   print("tick")
evidence_issues: godot-proposals #3936 '@override and super' (open, 51 reactions, 22 comments: 'I often forget to call super()') | godot-proposals #12310 (open, 15 reactions, 5 comments: 'Typos in overridden function names (like _proccess instead of _process) lead to hours of debugging') | godot-proposals #1631 must-override methods (open/reopened, 63 reactions, 11 comments; abstract methods added by PR #106409 in 4.5) | #29271 3.x implicit super-call inconsistency (closed 2020 for 4.0, 24 reactions, 16 comments)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html (Inheritance): "functions in extending classes replace functions with the same name in their super classes. If you still want to call them, you can use super" | same: "One of the common misconceptions is trying to override non-virtual engine methods such as get_class(), queue_free(), etc. This is not supported for technical reasons." (godot-docs 0914a4d gdscript_basics.rst:2332-2334,2354-2355)
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:1973-1977 (GDScriptInstance::callp returns at the first, most-derived match; base implementations are not called) vs modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:1992-2013 ('notification is not virtual, it gets called at ALL levels') | modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:1862-1872 (the parent-signature check runs only when a parent method of the same name exists, and only in TOOLS_ENABLED builds) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_warning.h:92,152 (NATIVE_METHOD_OVERRIDE, ERROR by default)
frequency: forum.godotengine.org exact phrases: "super._ready" 18 topics, "signature doesn't match the parent" 7 topics; the proposals above total 129 reactions
fix_reason: The compiler knows every engine virtual from extension_api.json (is_virtual/is_required, core/extension/extension_api_dump.cpp:1035-1037) and can require an override keyword and reject underscore methods that match no virtual; whether base callbacks chain is defined by the language's own script-instance call dispatch (GDExtensionScriptInstanceCall, core/extension/gdextension_interface.json:2860), which is public API.

title: Setter bypass applies only inside the accessor itself
description: Inside a property's own set/get the property name means the backing field, but any other function called from the setter goes through the setter again (infinite recursion; a hard crash before 4.0), and variable initializers are written directly without calling the setter, so setter side effects do not run for the initial value.
example: var hp := 10: ⏎   set(v): _apply(v) ⏎ func _apply(v): ⏎   hp = v  # re-enters the setter: infinite recursion
evidence_issues: #86494 'Setter function not called for default value' (closed not planned 2026-09, 12 reactions, 17 comments) | #48437 calling an external setter function from the setter block crashed with a stack overflow (closed by PR #72867 'Add limit to call depth' in 4.0, 5 reactions, 20 comments) | #62739 exported variables don't use their setters on initialisation (closed, 2 reactions, 2 comments)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html (When setter/getter is not called): "When a variable is initialized, the value of the initializer will be written directly to the variable. This occurs even if the @onready or @export annotation is applied to the variable." | same: "The exception does not propagate to other functions called in the setter/getter. For example, the following code will cause an infinite recursion" (godot-docs 0914a4d gdscript_basics.rst:2560-2561,2587-2588)
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript_compiler.cpp:1308 (direct member write only when the current function name equals the property's setter name) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_compiler.cpp:1364-1369 (otherwise the assignment calls the setter, including from helper functions) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:476-477 (MAX_CALL_DEPTH guard that turned the crash into an error)
frequency: #86494 17 comments; the rule needed its own docs subsection; no phrase-specific forum count
status: by-design, documented; crash replaced by a call-depth error in 4.0 (PR #72867)
fix_reason: The language can expose an explicit backing field usable anywhere in the class, define whether initializers run setters, and flag self-recursive setter paths statically; engine-side property writes still arrive through the script instance's set callback, which the language implements.

title: class_name lives in one flat global namespace
description: Every class_name is registered in a single project-wide namespace shared with native classes, autoloads and every addon; two addons using the same name, or a user class whose name a later engine version adds as a native class, fail to parse ('hides a global script class' / 'hides a native class'), and stale script-class cache entries after renames produce the same error.
example: # addons/a/state_machine.gd: class_name StateMachine ⏎ # addons/b/state_machine.gd: class_name StateMachine  # Parse Error: Class "StateMachine" hides a global script class.
root_layer: GDScript language (global class registry: engine core)
evidence_issues: godot-proposals #1566 'Implement namespaces in GDScript' (open, 363 reactions, 56 comments) | godot-proposals #4493 split class_name responsibility into two keywords (open, 43 reactions, 22 comments) | #67056 'hides a global script class' after renames (closed by PR #90186 in 4.3, 22 reactions, 34 comments) | #78642 invalid global_script_class_cache entries (closed, 11 reactions, 4 comments) | #99766 class_name tracker (open, 17 reactions, 0 comments)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html (Registering named classes): "Named classes are globally registered, which means they become available to use in other scripts without the need to load or preload them" (godot-docs 0914a4d gdscript_basics.rst:2170-2171)
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:400-407 (errors: hides a built-in type / native class / global script class / autoload singleton) | core/object/script_language.h:92 (ScriptServer::add_global_class keyed by one StringName: a single flat table for all languages) | core/object/script_language_extension.h:754 (_get_global_class_name: how an extension language registers its global names)
frequency: GraphQL search for "hides a global script class" in godotengine/godot: 39 issues/PRs (many are cache bugs); forum.godotengine.org exact phrase: 28 topics; #1566 is the 10th most-reacted topic:gdscript proposal
fix_reason: The language can have modules or namespaces and export only chosen names globally; anything registered for the editor, inspector or other languages goes into ScriptServer's flat global-class table and competes with ClassDB names, so collisions there remain an engine limitation.

title: get_class() and is_class() ignore class_name
description: For an object whose script declares class_name Player, get_class() returns the native base name and is_class("Player") is false, so code that dispatches on get_class() strings, or ports patterns from engine code, silently misidentifies script types (the working alternatives are 'is' and get_script().get_global_name()).
example: class_name Player extends CharacterBody2D ⏎ print(get_class())  # CharacterBody2D ⏎ print(is_class("Player"))  # false
evidence_issues: #21789 'get_class() and is_class() not returning class_name' (open, confirmed, 170 reactions, 63 comments; 29 cross-referencing issues) | #61396 (closed not planned, 2 reactions, 5 comments) | #60538 (closed, 0 reactions, 1 comment)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_object.html (get_class): "This method ignores class_name declarations. If this object's script has defined a class_name, the base, built-in class name is returned instead." (doc/classes/Object.xml:599, note added by PR #52614 in 4.0) | same page (is_class): "This method ignores class_name declarations in the object's script." (doc/classes/Object.xml:786)
evidence_source: core/object/object.h:677 (get_class() returns get_class_name(), the native ClassDB name; no script hook)
frequency: #21789 is the 2nd most-reacted topic:gdscript issue in godotengine/godot (GraphQL dump of 4377 issues sorted by reactions); 29 issues cross-reference it
fix_reason: The language provides its own type test and type name (is, script global name) and can warn on get_class()/is_class() with script class names; changing what Object::get_class returns for every caller (engine, other languages) needs an engine core change.

title: Cyclic dependencies between class_name and preload scripts
description: Scripts that reference each other through class_name types or preload() used to fail with cyclic-reference or 'could not resolve' errors (3.x); the 4.0 analyzer rewrite fixed the common cases, but loader-level cycles (preload cycles, autoload plus preload ordering, scene and resource cycles) still cause load failures.
example: # a.gd: class_name A, var b: B ⏎ # b.gd: class_name B, var a: A  # cyclic error in 3.x; accepted in 4.x
evidence_issues: #21461 'Some usages of class_name can produce cyclic errors unexpectedly' (closed by PR #67714 'Fix cyclic references in GDScript 2.0' in 4.0, high priority, 110 reactions, 81 comments; 33 cross-referencing issues) | #80877 cyclic dependencies tracker (open, 23 reactions, 6 comments; lists 52 linked issues, 30 still unchecked) | #80645 cyclic reference error with autoload, preload and ordering (open, 5 reactions, 3 comments) | godot-proposals #460 allow cyclic references (closed completed, 64 reactions, 20 comments)
evidence_source: unverified (cycle handling not traced in source for this catalog)
frequency: #21461 is the 5th most-reacted topic:gdscript issue (GraphQL dump of 4377 issues); forum.godotengine.org exact phrase "Cyclic reference": 39 topics (mixed with RefCounted reference cycles)
status: fixed for class_name type references in 4.0 (PR #67714); preload and resource cycles still open (tracker #80877)
fix_reason: A language that resolves all scripts of a module together can allow mutually recursive type references and avoid eager preload; cycles between resources and scenes go through ResourceLoader and remain engine behaviour.

title: Runtime errors abort only the current function; no exceptions
description: A GDScript runtime error (null access, invalid operands, failed typed assignment) stops only the current function, which returns a default value of its declared return type; the caller sees a successful call and continues with that value. In release export templates the checks and messages are compiled out, so execution continues silently with wrong data; there is no try/catch or error value to intercept failures, and engine API failures likewise just print and return a default.
example: func count() -> int: ⏎   var n: Node = null ⏎   return n.get_child_count()  # runtime error ⏎ var c := count()  # debug: error printed, c == 0, the caller keeps running
root_layer: GDScript language (engine ERR_FAIL convention: engine core)
evidence_issues: #3516 try/finally/except block for GDScript (closed, 21 reactions, 16 comments; maintainer: 'it's clear by now that exceptions won't be added to GDScript') | #7643 GDScript error checking (closed 2017, 13 reactions, 21 comments) | godot-proposals #4735 (closed, 2 reactions, 2 comments: 'It has already been stated that try-catch will never come into gdscript') | godot-proposals #3194 'Improve Errors and Error Handling for users' (open, 26 reactions, 4 comments) | #59239 return values always zero/null/false in the 4.0 release export (closed by PR #62317 in 4.0, 3 reactions, 7 comments)
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:474 (call error set to CALL_OK on entry; runtime errors never change it, so callers see success) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:3956-3979 (on error: print, debug_break, then 'Get a default return type in case of failure'; the whole block is under #ifdef DEBUG_ENABLED) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:1422-1432 (example of a runtime type check that exists only with DEBUG_ENABLED) | core/core_bind.cpp:870 and core/core_bind.h:139 (OS.add_logger / Logger._log_error: the public hook to observe engine errors, after the fact)
frequency: requested since 2016 (#3516) and recurring (#7643, #3194, #4735); no direct count of 'silently continued' reports
fix_class: L (engine part: W to observe, E to control flow)
fix_reason: The language defines its own failure semantics in its VM (abort the call chain, Result or error types, or exceptions, with checks kept in release builds); errors raised inside engine C++ methods (ERR_FAIL_* print and return a default) can only be observed globally through OS.add_logger, so turning them into script-level control flow needs an engine change.

title: No interfaces or traits: cross-hierarchy contracts fall back to duck typing
description: Classes that do not share a base class cannot declare a common typed contract, so code that handles 'anything damageable' uses has_method()/call() with string names or untyped calls, losing compile-time checking, completion and refactoring safety, or forces an artificial common base class.
example: if body.has_method("take_damage"): ⏎   body.take_damage(10)  # untyped; name typos unchecked
evidence_issues: godot-proposals #4872 'Allow explicitly defining interfaces in GDScript' (open, 830 reactions, 62 comments) | godot-proposals #6416 'Add a Trait system for GDScript' (open, 672 reactions, 242 comments) | #23101 'Add a GDScript Trait system.' (closed, 68 reactions, 93 comments) | godot-proposals #15448 'Formalize GDScripts as mixins' (open, 66 reactions, 12 comments)
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:6458-6507 (object type compatibility is decided only by walking native/script/class inheritance; there is no structural or interface relation)
frequency: #4872 and #6416 are the 4th and 5th most-reacted topic:gdscript proposals (GraphQL dump of 941 proposals sorted by reactions; 1502 reactions combined)
fix_reason: Interfaces or traits with static conformance checks are a language feature compiled by the language; whether engine-side consumers (other languages' type tests, inspector type filters on exports) could see a script-defined interface was not verified.

title: No generics; typed collections only one level deep
description: Only Array[T] and Dictionary[K, V] (4.4+) take type parameters, and only one level: Array[Array[int]], Dictionary[String, Array[int]], typed Callable/Signal signatures and user-defined generic classes are unsupported, so nested data (grids, maps of lists) is Variant inside and every inner access is unchecked.
example: var grid: Array[Array[int]]  # parse error: Nested typed collections are not supported.
root_layer: GDScript language (engine container type: engine core)
evidence_issues: godot-proposals #12224 nested typed arrays and dictionaries (open, 260 reactions, 12 comments; engine PR #107556 open) | godot-proposals #1207 generic parameters for collections (open, 241 reactions, 72 comments) | godot-proposals #10807 statically typed Callable (open, 141 reactions, 17 comments) | godot-proposals #2557 type hints for signal parameters (open, 134 reactions, 8 comments) | godot-proposals #56 typed dictionaries (closed, implemented by PR #78656 in 4.4, 836 reactions, 95 comments)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html (Typed arrays): "Nested array types (like Array[Array[int]]) are not supported." (godot-docs 0914a4d gdscript_basics.rst:882) | https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/static_typing.html: "Nested typed collections (like Dictionary[String, Dictionary[String, int]]) are not supported." (static_typing.rst:265-266)
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript_parser.cpp:3879 ('Nested typed collections are not supported.') | core/variant/container_type_validate.h:37-40 (the engine element type is variant_type + class_name + script, one level, no nested element type)
frequency: the 5 proposals total 1612 reactions; #56 (typed dictionaries) was the 3rd most-reacted GDScript proposal before it was implemented
fix_reason: The language can have generics checked statically and erase them to untyped engine containers at runtime; making nested element types visible to the engine (runtime validation, inspector, serialization, other languages) needs ContainerType to carry nested types, an engine core change (PR #107556).

title: Analyzer false-positive warnings push users to disable checks
description: Several warnings fire on correct code (a static function's parameter 'shadows' an instance member it cannot see; UNSAFE_* on autoloads and checked code; INTEGER_DIVISION even after an explicit cast) and @warning_ignore historically did not apply to every warning or statement, so users silence whole warning categories project-wide and lose them for real cases.
example: var speed := 1.0 ⏎ static func make(speed: float) -> void: pass  # SHADOWED_VARIABLE although static code cannot see the member
evidence_issues: #63120 static function argument reported as shadowing a member (open, confirmed, 28 reactions, 15 comments; 2 duplicates marked: #101840, #107572) | #42966 integer division warning after a cast (open, 60 reactions, 17 comments) | #56592 @warning_ignore does not work with all warnings (closed by PR #83037 in 4.3, 14 reactions, 21 comments) | #60499 false-positive UNSAFE_PROPERTY_ACCESS (open, 11 reactions, 6 comments; 1 duplicate) | #86300 UNSAFE_METHOD_ACCESS for .tscn autoloads (open, 12 reactions, 15 comments)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/warning_system.html: "Warnings won't prevent the game from running, but you can turn them into errors if you'd like." | same: "To ignore multiple warnings in a region within a file, use the @warning_ignore_start and @warning_ignore_restore annotations." (godot-docs 0914a4d warning_system.rst:34-36,47-48)
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:6173-6208 (is_shadowing checks class members without regard to whether the enclosing function is static) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:3161-3169 (INTEGER_DIVISION decided purely from operand static types, so int(x) / 2 still warns) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_parser.cpp:182-184 (@warning_ignore applies per class member or statement; region form @warning_ignore_start/@warning_ignore_restore)
frequency: the issues above total 125 reactions; #63120 and #60499 have 3 duplicates marked between them (GraphQL MARKED_AS_DUPLICATE events)
fix_reason: Diagnostics belong entirely to the new toolchain; a statically typed language needs fewer heuristic 'unsafe' warnings, and a separate integer-division operator removes the INTEGER_DIVISION ambiguity.
